title: 294. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Reflection Across the x-Axis
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the axis of reflection that produces \(y=-f(x)\) from \(y=f(x)\).
questions.question: The graph of \(y=-f(x)\) is the reflection of the graph of \(y=f(x)\) across which axis?
questions.explanation: For each point \((x,y)\) on the graph of \(y=f(x)\), the corresponding point on \(y=-f(x)\) is \((x,-y)\). This change negates only the \(y\)-coordinate, which is exactly reflection across the \(x\)-axis.
questions.hint: Compare how the \(x\)- and \(y\)-coordinates change when \(y\) is replaced by \(-y\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the image of a point on \(y=f(x)\) under reflection across the \(x\)-axis.
questions.question: The point \((3,4)\) lies on the graph of \(y=f(x)\). Which point lies on the graph of \(y=-f(x)\)?
questions.explanation:
Reflection across the \(x\)-axis keeps the \(x\)-coordinate and changes the sign of the \(y\)-coordinate. Thus \((3,4)\) maps to
\[
(3,-4)
\]
questions.hint: For reflection across the \(x\)-axis, negate the \(y\)-coordinate only.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the equation of \(y=x^2\) after reflection across the \(x\)-axis.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=x^2\) is reflected across the \(x\)-axis. What is the equation of the new graph?
questions.explanation:
Reflecting \(y=f(x)\) across the \(x\)-axis gives \(y=-f(x)\). With \(f(x)=x^2\), the new equation is
\[
y=-x^2
\]
questions.hint: Replace the entire function by its opposite.

questions.concept: Point Mapping Under Reflection Across the \(x\)-Axis
questions.learningObjective: Determine the image of a point under the transformation \(y=-f(x)\).
questions.question: The point \((2,5)\) lies on the graph of \(y=f(x)\). Which point lies on the graph of \(y=-f(x)\)?
questions.explanation:
For \(y=-f(x)\), the \(x\)-coordinate stays the same and the \(y\)-coordinate changes sign. Therefore, \((2,5)\) maps to
\[
(2,-5)
\]
questions.hint: Keep the \(x\)-coordinate fixed and negate the \(y\)-coordinate.

questions.concept: Recognizing a Reflection from an Equation
questions.learningObjective: Identify the reflection that changes \(y=(x+1)^2\) to \(y=-(x+1)^2\).
questions.question: The graph of \(y=-(x+1)^2\) is obtained from the graph of \(y=(x+1)^2\) by reflection across which axis?
questions.explanation: The equation \(y=-(x+1)^2\) has the form \(y=-f(x)\) with \(f(x)=(x+1)^2\). Replacing \(f(x)\) by \(-f(x)\) reflects the graph across the \(x\)-axis. Therefore, the reflection is across the \(x\)-axis.
questions.hint: Look at whether the negative sign is outside the entire function.

questions.concept: Point Mapping Under Reflection Across the \(x\)-Axis
questions.learningObjective: Determine the image of a point under the transformation \(y=-f(x)\).
questions.question: The point \((-2,3)\) lies on the graph of \(y=f(x)\). Which point lies on the graph of \(y=-f(x)\)?
questions.explanation:
Reflection across the \(x\)-axis keeps the \(x\)-coordinate and negates the \(y\)-coordinate. Thus \((-2,3)\) maps to
\[
(-2,-3)
\]
questions.hint: The sign of the \(y\)-value changes, but the \(x\)-value stays the same.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the equation after reflecting \(y=\sqrt{x}\) across the \(x\)-axis.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=\sqrt{x}\) is reflected across the \(x\)-axis. What is the equation of the new graph?
questions.explanation:
Reflection across the \(x\)-axis changes \(y=f(x)\) to \(y=-f(x)\). With \(f(x)=\sqrt{x}\), the reflected graph has equation
\[
y=-\sqrt{x}
\]
questions.hint: Reflection across the \(x\)-axis changes the sign of every output value of the function.

questions.concept: Recovering an Original Point from a Reflected Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine a point on \(y=f(x)\) from a point on \(y=-f(x)\).
questions.question: The point \((4,-1)\) lies on the graph of \(y=-f(x)\). Which point lies on the graph of \(y=f(x)\)?
questions.explanation:
The graph of \(y=-f(x)\) is the reflection of \(y=f(x)\) across the \(x\)-axis. Therefore, undoing the reflection changes the sign of the \(y\)-coordinate. The point \((4,-1)\) corresponds to
\[
(4,1)
\]
on \(y=f(x)\).
questions.hint: Reverse the sign change in the \(y\)-coordinate.

questions.concept: Reflecting a Quadratic Function Across the \(x\)-Axis
questions.learningObjective: Determine the equation of \(f(x)=x^2-2x\) after reflection across the \(x\)-axis.
questions.question: If \(f(x)=x^2-2x\), what is the equation of the graph after reflection across the \(x\)-axis?
questions.explanation:
Reflection across the \(x\)-axis gives \(y=-f(x)\). Since \(f(x)=x^2-2x\),
\[
y=-(x^2-2x)=-x^2+2x
\]
Therefore, the reflected graph has equation \(y=-x^2+2x\).
questions.hint: Multiply the entire expression for \(f(x)\) by \(-1\).

questions.concept: Determining an Original Function from Its Reflection
questions.learningObjective: Determine \(f(x)\) when the reflection \(y=-f(x)\) is given.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) is reflected across the \(x\)-axis to obtain the graph of \(y=2x-5\). What is \(f(x)\)?
questions.explanation:
The reflected graph is \(y=-f(x)\). It is given that this equals \(2x-5\); multiplying both sides by \(-1\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
-f(x) &= 2x-5\\
f(x) &= -(2x-5)\\
&= -2x+5
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, \(f(x)=-2x+5\).
questions.hint: Since the reflected equation equals \(-f(x)\), solve for \(f(x)\) by negating the entire expression.
